reps.name: Andrew Alonso
reps.headlineGap: The recording ends mid-evaluation, so the entire decision and close half of the visit is unverified.
focus: Week 1: Capture the full call — Every call recorded door-to-door. Review one complete recording with a manager end-to-end — specifically the presentation and any objection.
Week 2: The thermostat + bill pair — Ask the summer/winter setting deliberately on every HVAC call, always followed by the power-bill question. Manager spot-checks three calls.
Week 3: Membership in the Welcome — Address membership status before tools come out on every call. Track how many conversations it opens.

reps.name: Andrew Trujillo
reps.headlineGap: Both recordings stop during the intake, so no findings, options or close were captured on either call.
focus: Week 1: Capture the full call — Recorder check before every knock; recording stops only in the van. Review one complete call with a manager, focused on the presentation.
Week 2: Finish the expectations block — Five-star seed on every call, plus parking confirmed before entry and protectors down on entry. Manager spot-checks three calls.
Week 3: Filter frequency — Add the filter-change question to the intake he already runs, so all three critical HVAC questions are automatic.

reps.name: Benjamin Wyllie
reps.headlineGap: When customers ask what a replacement costs, he answers that pricing is a different department instead of proposing an appointment time.
focus: Week 1: Own the handoff — Replace the repair-guy line on every call. Manager reviews three recordings for the framing and for whether a time was proposed.
Week 2: Ask the bill before the analysis — Summer-and-winter setting plus the power-bill question on every HVAC call, before any efficiency number is mentioned.
Week 3: Collect the five-star — Seeded as he already does, then asked for on every call before leaving. Track seed-to-ask conversion.

reps.name: Brandon Moreno
reps.headlineGap: A direct question about replacement cost was answered with a rough estimate instead of a booked specialist visit.
focus: Week 1: The three required questions — Fixed block at the thermostat on every call: filter frequency, hot/cold rooms, summer-winter setting plus the power bill. Manager reviews three calls.
Week 2: Complete the expectations block — Add options, approval and today to the thorough-evaluation line he already gives. Role-play five times before Monday.
Week 3: Signal to slot — Every pricing question converts to a booked advisor appointment. Track how many signals appear and how many became slots.

reps.name: Cole Pantol
reps.headlineGap: Kept adding supporting arguments after the options were presented instead of stopping and letting the customer respond.
focus: Week 1: Zip It — Present options, deliver the closing line, then stay silent until the customer speaks. Manager reviews three recordings for post-ask talking.
Week 2: Filter + bill — Both missing required questions added to the thermostat block on every call, every time.
Week 3: Collect the five-star — Seed it in the Welcome as he already does, then ask for it before leaving on every call. Track seed-to-ask conversion.

reps.name: David Canales
reps.headlineGap: The specialist visit was offered three times across two calls and never converted into a booked appointment.
focus: Week 1: Signal to slot — Every price hesitation converts to a specialist appointment with a day and a time. Manager reviews three recordings for offers made versus slots booked.
Week 2: The three required questions — Fixed block at the thermostat on every call — filter frequency, hot/cold rooms, summer-winter setting plus the power bill.
Week 3: Photos and the five-star ask — Re-shoot any photo the customer cannot read before showing it, and ask for the review on every call before leaving.

reps.name: Francisco Valencia
reps.headlineGap: None of the required assessment questions were asked on any call, so the customer's own bill and comfort evidence never entered the conversation.
focus: Week 1: The three required questions — At the thermostat, every call, before tools. Manager reviews three recordings.
Week 2: One line, one number — Present each tier separately and pause. No compound figures. Role-play the HEWITT pricing conversation specifically.
Week 3: Seed and collect the five-star — In the expectations block on every call, asked for before leaving.

reps.name: Joe Mendoza
reps.headlineGap: Only one of the four required questions was asked across two calls, so both wins rested entirely on rapport and option-building.
focus: Week 1: The four required questions — Fixed block at the thermostat, every call. Manager reviews three recordings for all four.
Week 2: Do the reconnect — Ask the teach-back question and then actually deliver it. No talking himself out of it.
Week 3: Ask for the five-star — On every call, before leaving. He has the goodwill on nearly every visit; he just never collects.

reps.name: Juan Tlatenchi
reps.headlineGap: The specialist visit was offered as something the customer might want rather than proposed with a specific day and time.
focus: Week 1: The three required questions — Filter, rooms, and summer-winter temperature plus the power bill — at the thermostat, every call, in Spanish or English.
Week 2: Schedule, don't offer — Every specialist mention converts to a proposed day and time. Manager reviews three calls for offers versus bookings.
Week 3: Nothing leaves unscheduled — Repair date, specialist appointment or a specific callback time on every single visit. Track it.

reps.name: Mario Castro
reps.headlineGap: All three recordings end during the intake, so nothing after the questions was captured on any call.
focus: Week 1: Capture the full call — Recorder check before every knock; stops only in the van. Review one complete recording with a manager.
Week 2: The English expectations block — Approval and today added to every English call, matching what he already says in Spanish.
Week 3: Five-star seed — Planted on every call, both languages, then asked for at the close.

reps.name: Nathan Colquitt
reps.headlineGap: The expectations block covers only look and options, with no approval promise, today commitment or five-star standard.
focus: Week 1: The full expectations block — All six beats on every call. Role-play five times with a manager before Monday.
Week 2: Capture the full call — Recorder check before the knock, stops in the van. Review one complete recording end to end.
Week 3: The thermostat question — Ask summer and winter deliberately on every HVAC call, followed by the bill question he already asks well.

reps.name: Nikko April
reps.headlineGap: A customer volunteered that he wanted replacement pricing and received general advice instead of a booked specialist visit.
focus: Week 1: Signal to slot — Every replacement mention converts to a booked advisor appointment. Manager reviews both of these recordings with him first.
Week 2: Filter and bill — Both missing required questions added to every call, before the tools come out.
Week 3: Certainty discipline — No thinking out loud about facts you are unsure of. Name the limit, promise the follow-up, move on.

reps.name: Robert Silinzy
reps.headlineGap: Five visits ended with information delivered and nothing scheduled, including one where the customer asked directly about replacement cost.
focus: Week 1: Nothing leaves unscheduled — Every call ends with a repair date, an advisor appointment or a specific callback time. Track all five outcomes daily with a manager.
Week 2: The two missing questions — Summer-and-winter thermostat setting and hot-and-cold rooms added to the block he already runs well.
Week 3: Curiosity over correction — When a customer reasons back, respond with a question. Manager reviews two recordings for corrections versus questions.

skipped.reason: Recording ends about two minutes in, during the welcome; no assessment, options or outcome to grade.
Empty recording — no usable audio captured.
